thread.title: Apple Swats Mobile Gaming App Amid Debate Over Services Growth

author: REINHARDT KRAUSE
title: Apple Swats Mobile Gaming App Amid Debate Over Services Growth
text:
Apple ( AAPL ) has blocked the release of Steam Link — a free mobile gaming app created by the biggest distributor of PC-based video games — on its iPhones just as analysts clash over how much growth will be coming from the technology icon's services business.
X Bellevue, Wash.-based Valve, the biggest online store for downloaded games on Microsoft ( MSFT ) Windows PCs, said Friday that the Cupertino, Calif.-based company rejected the app. Valve recently released Steam Link on mobile phones using Google's Android software.
Apple collects a 30% cut from digital purchases at the App Store. Apple's services business includes the App Store as well as its music and pay applications. There's also its iCloud and other offerings.
The dispute raises questions over whether Apple could be developing its own streaming game service, said Ars Technica , a tech industry website.
 Morgan Stanley said Thursday the App Store will be the company's largest and most significant contributor to services growth. Apple shares were up slightly to close at 188.58 Friday.
Instinet, however, earlier said that the company's recent rally based on rosy forecasts for services business growth is misguided. Instinet says much of that estimated growth is already built into the stock price.
The iPhone maker has gained 16% since reporting earnings in late April. The stock is up 24% from a year ago amid slowing iPhone sales.
Apple Autonomous Strategy Loup Ventures on Thursday said that self-driving cars could also be part of the company's services business through partnerships with automakers .
"We believe Apple's end game is a software and services platform enabling autonomous mobility fleets," said Gene Munster, managing director of Loup Ventures, in a blog.
"The concept of an autonomous service is a departure from Apple's current hardware and content services business," Munster went on to say. "Specifically, delivering their experience through third-party hardware is a strategy that Apple rarely employs. That said, we believe, given the complexities of manufacturing a car (just ask Tesla ( TSLA )) and the size of the opportunity, it makes sense for Apple to partner their way to autonomy."
In other company news, Samsung must pay Apple $539 million for infringing five patents with Android phones it sold in 2010 and 2011. The ruling from a U.S. District Court jury in San Jose, Calif., stems from a legal battle that dates back to 2011.
In another case, court documents reveal that Apple's iPhone 6 and 6 Plus phones were more likely to bend than previous models. The website Motherboard reported the findings.
